items.title: Bug fixes and performance improvements.
The web app is withdrawn until further notice.
items.detail: Kyron is the Android and Windows apps; the website's "Log In" and sign-up buttons now lead to the download page, and old links to the web app land there too.

items.title: Passwords found in data breaches are turned away.
items.detail: Signing up or setting a password checks it against the Have I Been Pwned list of leaked passwords (only the first five characters of its fingerprint leave your phone), and asks for a different one if it is there.

items.title: The website sends headers that stop it being framed or content-sniffed, and the API no longer accepts calls from any web page.
Staff accounts can turn on two-step sign-in with an authenticator app, and the API can require it for moderation tools (STAFF_REQUIRE_SECOND_FACTOR).
The last English screens are translated.
items.detail: Sign-up's password rules, the profile tabs, verification, the voice recorder, the "not ready yet" screens, About, error reports, contact support, text size, appearance, muted and blocked accounts and the password screen now read in all 68 languages.

items.title: Deleting your account asks you to confirm it's you.
items.detail: If you last signed in a while ago, Kyron asks for your password (or Google) first, so an unlocked phone is not enough to erase an account.

items.title: Blocking holds everywhere.
items.detail: Someone you blocked, or who blocked you, can no longer like, repost, save, quote, vote on or reply to your posts and comments, and hiding one post no longer empties your feed.

items.title: Deleted posts' pictures go too.
items.detail: Photos and clips of a deleted post are removed 30 days later, after any report or appeal about it has had time.

items.title: Signing out no longer loses your messages.
items.detail: Signing out, or a refresh that failed for want of signal, deleted this phone's message key along with the session, so messages sent to you before showed as "Waiting for this message".

items.title: Your sign-in is kept in the phone's keystore, not in a plain file, and Kyron is left out of backups and phone-to-phone transfers.
Links in the in-app browser ask before opening another app, and can never open Kyron itself or an app's internals.

A security review's findings on the server: link previews can no longer be steered at private addresses, uploads are checked by their contents, profile fields have limits, message keys are capped per account, rate limits and CORS are stricter, the old sign-in endpoints are removed, and the server runs as an unprivileged user.
Kyron now speaks your language everywhere.
items.detail: The buttons, menus, empty screens and error messages that were still in English are now translated in all 68 languages, and the language screen no longer claims parts of the app stay in English.

items.title: Back takes you Home, not out.
items.detail: From Explore, Communities or Messages, back goes to Home; on Home, it asks for a second press before Kyron closes, so a stray back never leaves the app.

items.title: See who gave a post its gifts.
items.detail: Tap the gift pill: everyone who sent one, the biggest giver first and named as such, with what they sent.

items.title: Every part of a notification opens its own page.
items.detail: A face or a name opens that person, the picture opens the post, and a reply's words open the reply.

items.title: What's new, after each update, once, so you can see what changed.
A quick check-in on your third and tenth day: one tap on a face, and a line if you have something to say.
Reminders, now and then.
items.detail: After a day and a half away, an evening note about what's new, only if something is; and on Monday, a note that your gift coins are back, if you spent some.

items.title: Full-width buttons are the login button's size.
items.detail: They were 8 points taller and heavier than it, across settings, sheets and moderation screens; every one is now exactly the same 40-point pill.

items.title: A profile's tabs sit on the page in the dark theme, not on a grey band across it, and the ring round the profile picture is the page's black instead of grey.
